messages.subject: One Visit SECR possibility?
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

As I am reading through all the SECR literature, it seems like there wold be a possibility to estimate the population from one capture session.

Does this extend to one visit (one fecal sampling day/attempt)?

In my example, fecal samples would be collected along transects and analyzed to individual level. In the past, there has been recaptures of the same individual within one visit to the site. Would this be able to be reliably run through SECR to obtain density estimates?

I appreciate any input/advice!
Thank you!
-Carson M

messages.subject: Re: One Visit SECR possibility?
messages.body_plain:
Yes. That was the point of Efford, Dawson and Borchers 2009 Ecology 90:2676 in which we said "Single sample analytical methods also enable novel field designs. For example, a set of grid cells may be searched
for fecal samples attributable to individual animals by analysis of microsatellite DNA...". However, it may be hard to collect enough data along transects, and, as always, the transects should be representative of the study area.

messages.body_plain:
Thank you for the quick replies!

That paper has been extremely helpful in my search! My transects are also less traditional in the sense they are transects walked across the entire suitable habitat and searched for pellet samples.

What modifications need to be made in the Rcode to compliment the one visit sampling data?

I currently have been using a transect proximity detector with a polygon mask with a hazard half normal function.
Here is a short summary of that:
KettleTransectCH<- read.capthist(captfile="Kettle2018Capt.csv", trapfile= "Kettle2018ProxTrap.csv",
                             detector = "proximity",
                             fmt ="XY",
                             skip=1)

This has worked in the past with two visits, so I am hoping to try it without the second visit and compare the results.

Thank you,
Carson M

messages.subject: Optimal mask spacing when using fine-scale covariates
messages.subject_clean: Optimal mask spacing when using fine-scale covariates
messages.body_plain:
Hello secr group,

I’m preparing to run an analysis with detection data on transects. My goal is to model inhomogeneous snowshoe hare densities as a function of forest characteristics. My forest covariate data layers (rasters) can be very fine scale if I want them to be. I currently have rasters with pixel size of 10-30 meters depending on the layer. My study area is large (10 smaller study areas at 4 sq km each = 40 sq km total). I expect sigma to be around 200 meters.

My question is about optimal mask spacing. The secr-habitatmasks.pdf recommends mask spacing less than sigma, such as 0.6*sigma, but this is for uniform density models, and I am modeling inhomogeneous density with fine-scale landscape data. If I make mask spacing much larger than my finest-scale raster (10 meters), then the mask cells will encompass multiple raster pixels. My understanding is that only the value directly under the mask cell center point is assigned to the mask cell. So if a hare was detected in dense understory, but the mask cell center overlaps a pixel with open understory, then I’ve completely lost the forest context that the detection was in.

Ideally, I could use a mask spacing the same as my raster such that mask cells and raster pixels (mostly) align, but for my large area that will be an infeasible number of mask points. I’ve tested this process with a mask spacing of 60 meters and processing times are already 3-12 hours depending on complexity of the model.

I want to minimize mask points while ensuring I get quality estimates for the coefficients and for density. I ran a loop fitting the same model across mask spacings from 5 to 100 meters, comparing estimates to known population size of the simulated population. The results of this showed fairly stable estimates for realized population size, that were near truth.

This seems to suggest that mask spacing won’t affect my estimates much. However, I just can’t get over the feeling that a mask spacing of 60 meters or so is going to change the relationships estimated between hare density and forest characteristics like understory density.

Am I correctly understanding how the mask uses covariate data? Should I take the simulations to mean that mask spacing won’t affect my results? I could use some guidance here, if anyone has any thoughts on this!

Thank you,
Amanda

messages.subject: Re: Optimal mask spacing when using fine-scale covariates
messages.subject_clean: Optimal mask spacing when using fine-scale covariates
messages.body_plain:
Hi Amanda,

Few thoughts: You're right that secr evaluates the raster at the mask point and uses that as the covariate ("addCovariates") but you can manipulate the underlying raster to be whatever resolution you like. I think often it makes more sense to do some aggregation so that the covariate represents some summary of the vicinity of the mask point rather than the value exactly at the point (or whatever the highest resolution is). This is especially for wide-ranging animals where mask points may be a few km apart (seems unlikely that it is only conditions right at the mask point that matter).

As far as I know there is no clear guidance on what to use as "in the vicinity" or how to summarize the values. The mask spacing is a natural choice (so the covariate is the average value in the mask cell) but not the only option. Likewise whether you summarize with an average, max/min, etc probably depends on context - average is a reasonable default. This must be an issue for other kinds of spatial models so maybe some guidance is available elsewhere but I suspect the answer is that there is no correct answer.

As for the spacing itself, using inhomogenous models shouldn't matter. The mask defines possible places animals can have activity centers and is just a computational device that allows the likelihood to be calculated and maximized, whether density varies spatially or not. The flat line in your figure is probably because these are all fine spacings (if you used sigma = 200) though the consistent small bias is a bit weird.

Last thing is potential confusion between mask covariates and detector covariates. If hares are (say) more likely to be detected in forest then that would be modelled with a detector covariate (lambda0 ~ forest) rather than a mask covariate. Here the raster aggregation issue might not apply because maybe it is conditions right at the detector that matter.

Hope that helps or that others correct me if I'm wrong.

Ian

messages.subject_clean: Problems with run.scenarios on a linear mask
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,
I am trying to use run.scenarios using a linear mask (attachment) and a non-Euclidean function.
I tried not to specify this in the code as the vignette says it (userdist = networkdistance) is default with a linear mask.

However, I get such a warning message for some scenarios (I am using 1 rep per scenario and only 12 rows to speed it up):

sims <- run.scenarios (1, scenarios = scens[1:12,],
                       trapset = simtraps, maskset = riversmask,
                       pop.args = list(model2D = 'linear'),
                       fit = TRUE, extractfn = predict, fit.function = 'secr.fit',
                       ncores = 12, byscenario = FALSE, seed = 345)
...
24: In (function (capthist, model = list(D ~ 1, g0 ~ 1, sigma ~ ... : using Euclidean distances with linear mask

Hence, I tried putting it in the det.args:

arg <- list(userdist = networkdistance)

sims <- run.scenarios (1, scenarios = scens[1:12,],
                       trapset = simtraps, maskset = riversmask,
                       det.args = list(arg),
                       pop.args = list(model2D = 'linear'),
                       fit = TRUE, extractfn = predict, fit.function = 'secr.fit',
                       ncores = 12, byscenario = FALSE, seed = 345)

However, I still get the same warning for some scenarios.

Finally, I tried using the fit.args and I get an error

arg <- list(userdist = networkdistance)

sims <- run.scenarios (1, scenarios = scens[1:12,],
                       trapset = simtraps, maskset = riversmask,
                       fit.args = list(arg),
                       pop.args = list(model2D = 'linear'),
                       fit = TRUE, extractfn = predict, fit.function = 'secr.fit',
                       ncores = 12, byscenario = FALSE, seed = 345)

Error in f(x, ...) : unused argument (userdist = function (xy1, xy2, geometry) { if (missing(xy1)) return(character(0)) rn <- list(rownames(xy1), rownames(xy2)) if (is.null(dim(xy1))) xy1 <- matrix(xy1, ncol = 2) if (is.null(dim(xy2))) xy2 <- matrix(xy2, ncol = 2) if (missing(geometry)) geometry <- xy2 gr <- attr(geometry, "graph") if (is.null(gr)) gr <- asgraph(geometry) geometryxy <- cbind(V(gr)$x, V(gr)$y) matchedxy1 <- nearesttrap(xy1, geometryxy) matchedxy2 <- nearesttrap(xy2, geometryxy) uniquematchedxy1 <- unique(matchedxy1) tmp <- t(igraph::shortest.paths(gr, weights = NULL, v = matchedxy2, to = uniquematchedxy1)) rematch <- match(matchedxy1, uniquematchedxy1) tmp <- tmp[rematch, , drop = FALSE] if (!("weight" %in% igraph::list.edge.attributes(gr))) tmp <- tmp * spacing(geometry) dimnames(tmp) <- rn tmp }) In addition: There were 13 warnings (use warnings() to see them) Error in UseMethod("predict") : no applicable method for 'predict' applied to an object of class "try-error"

Mymask has an issue, it consists of 4 separate systems. Considering real data, individuals do not move across systems and thus "networkdistance" can be used. Perhaps in simulated scenarios, individuals are fabricated with detections across systems causing an issue in the model?

Thank you very much

Stefano

Hi Stefano

It always helps to provide a simple example. This works for me ('tho maybe not an ideal example):

library(secrlinear)
library(secrdesign)
scen <- make.scenarios(D = 30, g0 = 0.07, sigma = 50)
sims <- run.scenarios (5, scenarios = scen,
                       trapset = traps(arvicola), maskset = glymemask,

                       pop.args = list(model2D = 'linear'),

                       fit.args = list(details = list(userdist = networkdistance)),
                       fit = TRUE, seed = 123)

Network distance is not the default, as should have been clear from the vignette. I see -

"We can fit a spatially explicit model to the water vole data in
three ways: (i) ignoring the linearity of the habitat (fit2DEuc), (ii)
with a linear habitat map and the default Euclidean distance model
(fit1DEuc), or (iii) with both linear habitat and an appropriate
non-Euclidean distance function (fit1DNet):"

Is the default stated differently somewhere else?

A spurious warning
mean.default(full.pop.args[[pi]]$D) : argument is not numeric or logical: returning NA
can be ignored, or avoided by setting D in pop.args. I have fixed it for the next version of secrdesign.

Murray

Prompted by Stefano off-list...

You are quite right about the default distance function in run.scenarios for linear masks: there is a major error in the documentation (section 'Linear habitat' of secrdesign-vignette.pdf). I can see nothing in the code that implements networkdistance as the default.

I'm wondering how best to resolve this. It's easy to fix the vignette, and maybe provide a correct example. The trouble with making networkdistance the default in the package is that there are two places it might apply (data simulation, model fitting) and it's nice to allow these to be different, under user control as at present. Also, that vignette is not distributed with the package, so I wouldn't have to submit a new version of secrdesign. So I guess I'll just correct the vignette.

I put a new version of secrlinear on CRAN this week in response to your earlier point, but the Windows binary won't appear there for another day.

Murray
